This year has officially become the year of the super-app. OpenAI recently launched its own super-app and admitted the program was "a bit of a mess." Microsoft CEO has also confirmed that a Copilot super-app will be released soon.

Microsoft Copilot "super-app" will integrate Cowork, chat, coding and other features

Microsoft is developing an AI "super-app" that integrates Copilot's chat, coding and agentic features. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch this year, covering "consumer and commercial experiences." Nadella said: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork and then to Autopilots. This quarter, we are integrating these Copilot experiences, including coding, into one super-app... This is a major step forward and I look forward to sharing more details later."

OpenAI's own "super-app" launch has turned into a debacle, but that evidently has not deterred other companies from continuing to pursue the super-app strategy.

Perhaps Microsoft is better positioned to deliver a do-it-all app without repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella has also recently said the company is shifting from apps toward a focus on agents. The AI era is still in its early stages, and the trends and best practices for building AI-centric interfaces are constantly evolving.

As for Apple, there are no signs that it will shift toward super-apps; instead, it continues to roll out new and specialised standalone apps. Whether it will change this strategy in the future remains to be seen.

What do you think of the recent "super-app" craze? Let us know in the comments.
